text.en: Healthy habits begin with knowing what harms us. In this lesson we learn about abuse, addiction and how a person can recover with support.

Abuse means cruel, violent or harmful treatment of another person; types are physical, emotional, verbal, sexual and child abuse.
Children are soft targets because they may not realise they are being abused; abusers are often known to the child and may lure with gifts.
Protection: the POCSO Act 2012 protects children from sexual offences and sets up special courts; Child Helpline 1098 offers help; NCPCR was set up in 2007.
A child should never accept gifts from people without parents' knowledge and should tell a trusted adult about any unsafe touch.
Care of an abused child: helpline, counselling, family support, medical care, legal counsel, rehabilitation and community awareness.
Addiction is physical and mental dependency on drugs, alcohol or tobacco; psychotropic drugs alter behaviour and WHO (1984) suggested the term drug dependence.
Warning signs: falling grades, loss of interest in hygiene, isolation, change in food and sleep habits and aggressive behaviour.
De-addiction has detoxification, psychotherapy, counselling of the family and rehabilitation; the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act was passed in 1985.
Tobacco contains nicotine; smoke causes lung cancer, bronchitis, emphysema, hypoxia through carbon monoxide, ulcers and oral cancer; the Anti Tobacco Act is of 2004.
Alcohol depresses the nervous system, damages nerve cells and the liver (fatty liver, cirrhosis) and causes accidents; recovery needs education, activity, family help and medical care.

problem.en: Why does carbon monoxide in tobacco smoke cause hypoxia?

text.en: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells.

why.en: It binds more strongly than oxygen.

text.en: Low oxygen in tissues is hypoxia.

prompt.en: List the steps of drug de-addiction in order.

points.en: Abuse and addiction harm body and mind; help exists: helpline 1098.
De-addiction: detoxification, psychotherapy, family counselling, rehabilitation.
Tobacco and alcohol harm lungs, heart and liver.
